checked_claims.claim: Reversibility preflight prevents any partial rollback across composite operations
checked_claims.reason: Top-level phase checks reversible but SeparateDatabaseAndState invokes nested backwards directly; universal preflight guarantee is unsupported.

tasks.notes: Static source review of central claims; no repository execution.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: Migration.unapply first checks each top-level operation.reversible and builds intermediate states, raising IrreversibleError before its second phase executes backwards operations (django/db/migrations/migration.py:139-170). Operations supply polymorphic reversible properties; IrreversibleError derives from RuntimeError (django/db/migrations/exceptions.py:34-35). This is local preflight, not a guarantee that every nested operation or entire migration plan is reversible: SeparateDatabaseAndState delegates backwards execution directly to contained operations (django/db/migrations/operations/special.py:43-58). Transaction scope and backend behavior determine rollback of changes if execution later fails.

checked_claims.reason: Preparation validates before binding SQL value but may occur inside existing atomic scope; no universal transaction timing guarantee.

tasks.notes: Static source review of central claims; no repository execution.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: UUIDField.get_db_prep_value converts non-UUID values through to_python, returning a UUID for native support or hex otherwise. Invalid string/integer representations caught by to_python raise ValidationError (django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:2753-2774). Keeping this conversion provides a common field-level error before SQL execution, but does not place the error outside transactions: preparation can occur inside an existing atomic block, whose exception handling governs rollback (django/db/transaction.py:224-303). Deferring validation to a database would make behavior backend-dependent, particularly where UUIDs are stored as text.

checked_claims.reason: Cached values bypass descriptor on subsequent access; choices/settings/backend-dependent properties are mutable/contextual, and performance magnitude is unmeasured.

material_errors: Cached values bypass descriptor on subsequent access; choices/settings/backend-dependent properties are mutable/contextual, and performance magnitude is unmeasured.
tasks.notes: Static source review of central claims; no repository execution.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: Non-cached properties can repeat work: flatchoices rebuilds a list, db_tablespace consults current settings, and db_returning uses current connection features (django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:928-937,1093-1096). Cached properties store results in instance.__dict__, bypassing their descriptor thereafter (django/utils/functional.py:39-48). Source alone does not establish a regression or its size. Profile actual hot paths before optimizing; unconditional caching needs invalidation because choices can be reassigned and settings/connection context can change (django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:548-554).

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: The chain is House.only("name") -> Prefetch("rooms", Room.prefetch_related(Prefetch("house", House.only("address")))) (tests/prefetch_related/tests.py:1975-1995). When iterating the child queryset, the reverse manager only fills Room.house if that field is not already cached (django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py:762-769). set_cached_value itself simply assigns (django/db/models/fields/mixins.py:30-31). The inner only clause makes different field loading visible in the regression test; removing it still fetches address and does not disable cache protection or inherently break the zero-query address access.

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: Field.clean converts, validates requiredness, then runs validators in that order (django/forms/fields.py:200-208). Exceptions from to_python or validate immediately abort later steps. run_validators skips empty values and collects validator errors (django/forms/fields.py:182-198). Large workloads repeat these operations, but the source does not demonstrate a performance regression. Profile conversion and validators before optimizing, and preserve normalization order, errors and validation semantics; blindly skipping unchanged fields or caching conversions can change results.

checked_claims.claim: Formset.save is automatically atomic and dropping uniqueness requires duplicate cleanup
checked_claims.reason: No atomic wrapper here; Model.save does not automatically run full_clean. Dropping uniqueness does not require duplicate cleanup; adding uniqueness does.

material_errors: No atomic wrapper here; Model.save does not automatically run full_clean. Dropping uniqueness does not require duplicate cleanup; adding uniqueness does.
tasks.notes: Static source review of central claims; no repository execution.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: AbstractUser.username declares unique=True (django/contrib/auth/models.py:454-467). Model/form validation can detect duplicates early, while the database constraint protects against concurrent races. BaseModelFormSet.save saves existing/new objects without wrapping the whole batch in atomic (django/forms/models.py:798-814); all-or-nothing behavior requires an enclosing transaction, handled by Atomic.__exit__ (django/db/transaction.py:224-303). Removing the database constraint permits duplicate writes even if model metadata remains unique; changing metadata too changes validation and may trigger auth uniqueness checks (django/contrib/auth/checks.py:71-99). Dropping the constraint does not itself require duplicate cleanup; reintroducing uniqueness after duplicates arise does.
